title: Middleware order and centralized errors
summary: Parse JSON, validate before the handler, and delegate failures to a four-argument error handler.

scenario.briefing: The product API accepts new products. A request without a valid body reached the store, and a thrown validation error produced an empty response because the error handler never ran.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Register express.json() before the route that reads the body.
Validate both name and price in a middleware function.
Call next(error) with a status and code instead of writing the response.
Keep the error handler last and give it all four parameters.

misconceptions.description: Registering the error handler before the routes.
misconceptions.feedback: Error middleware only sees failures from middleware and routes registered before it. Register it after them.
misconceptions.diagnostic: A four-argument handler registered before the route never receives that route's failures.

misconceptions.description: Answering a validation failure inside the middleware.
misconceptions.feedback: That bypasses the shared error contract. Pass the error with next(error) and let the boundary serialize it.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Writing the response inside validation bypasses the shared error contract.

misconceptions.description: Shipping a middleware chain with the error handler first.
misconceptions.feedback: A four-argument handler registered before the route never sees later failures. Parser and validation order are also wrong, so the change is blocked.

sections.title: Middleware runs in order
sections.body: Each app.use and route registration joins a chain. A parser registered after a route cannot prepare the body for that route, so shared work belongs before the handlers that need it. Authentication belongs before validation so an anonymous request is rejected before its body is inspected.

sections.title: next(error) skips to the error handler
sections.body: Calling next() continues the normal chain. Calling next(error) skips the remaining normal middleware and finds the next four-argument handler.

sections.title: Four arguments identify an error handler
sections.body: Express detects an error handler by its arity. It must be registered after the routes it protects and must keep all four parameters even if next is unused.

steps.title: Validate JSON before the handler
steps.prompt: Edit app.ts. Add express.json() with a size limit, validate name and price in middleware, call next(error) on invalid input, and register a four-argument error handler after the routes.

tests.description: The JSON parser is registered before the routes with a size limit.

artifact.title: app.ts
artifact.caption: The error handler is registered first, the parser is registered last, and validation answers on its own.

findings.label: The error handler is registered before the route, so Express never calls it for a later failure.
The validation branch answers directly instead of calling next(error).
express.json() is registered after the route, so request.body is undefined there.
The error handler keeps internal messages out of the response.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the middleware order and delegation are fixed.
Ship it; Express resolves this order safely.

steps.explanation: Express only invokes a four-argument handler when it appears after the failing route and receives next(error). Here the handler is registered first, the JSON parser runs after the route, and validation writes its own response instead of delegating.
hints: Trace the registration order from top to bottom.
Check whether the parser runs before the route reads the body.
Check whether validation delegates with next(error).
Ignore findings that are not present and block on order and delegation.
